summary_rationale: Netweb Technologies is a genuinely profitable, fast-growing Indian high-end computing OEM with a narrow but real qualification-and-integration moat. Revenue compounded at roughly 50% a year for eight years to ₹2,184 crore in FY2026; operating margin has held at 13–14% even as scale multiplied; ROCE of 37.5% and ROE of 32.9% comfortably exceed an estimated 12–14% cost of capital; the balance sheet is net-debt-negative with ₹403 crore of unutilised QIP proceeds; and the confirmed order book of ₹2,629 crore rose even after ₹2,143 crore of H1 FY27 billing. It is classified CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL rather than COMPOUNDER_PASS for three evidence-based reasons. First, cash conversion has been poor: from FY2021 to FY2025 Netweb reported roughly ₹382 crore of cumulative profit against about ₹27 crore of operating cash flow, and FY2026's healthy ₹171 crore of operating cash flow only restored a 0.83x conversion ratio. Second, the revenue mix has shifted decisively toward AI systems (58.4% of Q2 FY27 revenue), where competition from global OEMs and Taiwanese ODMs is fiercest, gross margin is structurally thinner and demand is tied to one of the most volatile capital-expenditure cycles in modern markets. Third, the growth is financed by a working-capital engine, not a factory: inventory days rose from 86 to 117 and the cash-conversion cycle lengthened from 84 to 94 days, so a stall in pipeline conversion would convert inventory into a write-down before it showed up as a revenue miss. The business is real, the earnings are audited and the customers are creditworthy — but the durability of the earnings depends on a demand cycle the company does not control. KPI health is PASS_WITH_WATCH: the order book, pipeline, margin framework and repeat-customer retention are all healthy, but the inventory build and lengthening cash cycle are the specific metrics to monitor every quarter. No cash-flow, related-party or accounting-integrity red flag warrants a FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL.
